Final full-block clock in the installed native VM; visually inspected

behavior: Login reads the system local time outside the pure shared presentation crate.
The large clock shares the logo header and leaves the full form visible at 80 by 25.
Only ASCII and full blocks are used: the installed console font lacks the compressed half-block glyphs.
The lock clock is explicitly a static Locked at time, prepared once before vlock starts.
The fixed message mode does not open a terminal, read stdin, or contact greetd. The integration test keeps stdin open without supplying a byte.
Missing, failed, untrusted, slow, oversized or invalid message output falls back to the original lock message.
Only Debian vlock/PAM reads unlock credentials; no clock thread or redraw runs during authentication.
The native renderer releases acquired VT ownership to automatic switching instead of replaying a previous process-controlled mode.
Each old scanout row remains visible until its replacement is copied; only row padding and unused rows are cleared.
full_suite: Focused checkpoint only. rc10-native-input.json retains the earlier full summary and named missing-runtime failures. Final release qualification is pending.
limits: The lock clock intentionally shows lock-start time, not a ticking current-time claim.
The installed debug VMs have no NIC and use disposable overlays and generated credentials; no owner laptop or book was used.
HP Stream font, local-time and small-screen checks remain on HARDWARE_CHECKLIST.md.
The clock screens are not final package/update/boot-image qualification. Fades, picture splash and wider test-driver work are still pending.
The renderer measurement checkpoint precedes these interface changes and must not be treated as final release measurements.
The native renderer still uses one scanout buffer. Removing the clear does not establish tear-free physical scanout.
